summary: Lockless per-run JSON registry (under the external artifact base) that lets concurrent z-harness sessions discover each other's plans, seed likely file scope via a Haiku scope-extractor, and advisorily coordinate via a per-file claim/release/wait-for lease mechanism; overlap is always advisory except one strict-mode hard gate.

entry_points.summary: session-id subcommand: prints stable session id. Returns $Z_HARNESS_SESSION_ID if set; else derives <ppid>-<start_epoch> (Linux /proc; macOS pure-Python fallback). Always exits 0.

register subcommand: creates/overwrites <active>/<run-id>.json atomically via tmpfile+os.replace. Validates run_id safe basename. Idempotent. Emits plan_registered. Returns 0 on success, 3 on failure (LOUD). Accepts optional --watchdog-pid, but no current caller passes it (currently inert field).

heartbeat subcommand: updates last_heartbeat/phase/current_task/status in own record. If record absent (reaped or never registered), emits registry_error(reason:missing_record) and returns 0 — does NOT fabricate zombie record. NON-FATAL always returns 0. There is no --waiting-on CLI flag; the paused-beat combined atomic write of status=paused + waiting_on is performed internally by _set_waiting_on() inside wait-for's poll loop.
update-scope subcommand: merges scope array [{path, confidence, reason}] into own record. Paths stored as-is (caller normalizes). NON-FATAL — always returns 0, self-logs registry_error on failure.
list subcommand: returns all records (live and stale). --json flag for machine-readable output.

deregister subcommand: atomic unlink of <active>/<run-id>.json. FileNotFoundError is benign (no registry_error). Genuine OSError self-logs registry_error. Emits plan_deregistered. NON-FATAL always returns 0. Also invokes _sigterm_watchdog() (currently always a no-op — no .watchdog.pid file is ever written in production).

claim subcommand: stage-then-check-after-claim per-file lease acquisition. Stages paths in memory, re-reads all peer records (F2), applies lexicographic run_id tiebreak (lower run_id = senior wins any contended path). Persists only the WON set into held_paths — loser record MUST NOT contain the conceded path. Stdout: JSON {claimed:[...], conceded:[{path, holder_run_id}]}. Emits lease_claimed. Exit 0 always (advisory). Z_HARNESS_REGISTRY_ENABLED=0 → silent no-op.

release subcommand: remove named paths (--paths p1,p2) or all paths (--all) from own held_paths. Best-effort, always exits 0. Emits lease_released {run_id, paths}. Z_HARNESS_REGISTRY_ENABLED=0 → silent no-op.

wait-for subcommand: park current run behind senior peer(s) until their records clear or budget expires. Drops non-senior or absent targets immediately. Poll loop (Z_HARNESS_WAIT_POLL_SECS): single atomic write status=paused+waiting_on (via _set_waiting_on, preserving held_paths), runs reap inline via _reap_inline(), rechecks targets. Emits wait_started, wait_cleared (exit 0), wait_timeout (exit 10), wait_interrupted (exit 130). waiting_on cleared on EVERY exit path via finally — no paused zombies.

overlaps subcommand: path intersection of own scope vs all other live records. JSON payload includes a 'peers' array (per-peer scope overlaps) and a top-level 'held_conflict' flat array ({path, peer_run_id, holder_seniority}) for held-path intersections across all live lease-capable peers. held_conflict is absent when no held-path conflicts exist — it is NOT nested inside peer entries. Exit codes: 0 none; 10 advisory; 20 blocking (strict mode AND explicit×explicit exact path match with live peer). Same session_id → skipped.

reap subcommand: (a) host=localhost AND pid dead → delete immediately; live-local-pid carve-out: host=localhost AND pid confirmed alive AND past 2× stale → mark status:stale, do NOT delete (deferred until pid dies); (b) past 2× stale margin AND no live-local-pid → delete (remote/unknown-host, missing/non-int pid); (c) remote/unknown host past 1× → mark status:stale only. NON-FATAL overall. Emits plan_reaped / plan_marked_stale. _reap_inline() (line 1532) duplicates the logic for use inside wait-for's poll loop without re-resolving active_plans_dir.

Helper: returns True iff record has schema_version >= 2 AND held_paths field present. Non-numeric schema_version → False (lease-incapable). Missing held_paths NEVER interpreted as 'holds nothing'. v1 records contribute to soft scope overlap only, never to held-path waiting.
Helper: returns True iff peer_run_id < my_run_id (lexicographic). Canonical seniority predicate — started_at is display-only and MUST NOT be used for ordering. Non-str argument → False.

Helper: atomically write status + waiting_on in a single tmpfile+os.replace, preserving held_paths and refreshing last_heartbeat. Called inside wait-for poll loop to guarantee no window where status=paused but waiting_on is stale (MINOR-1). Empty list clears waiting_on.

Helper: builds a fresh schema-v2 record dict. schema_version=2, includes held_paths:[] and waiting_on:[] fields, plus a watchdog_pid field (currently always None/inert in production — no caller populates it). v1 records (pre-lease) lack held_paths/waiting_on and are treated as lease-incapable by _is_lease_capable.
Helper: same reap logic as cmd_reap but called inside wait-for's poll loop. Takes an already-resolved active_dir and stale_threshold to avoid a redundant plan-path.sh call on every poll iteration.

Five-tier base resolution with anchor enforcement. Tier 1: Z_HARNESS_BASE_DIR (bypass anchor, TRUE ESCAPE HATCH). Tiers 2-4 active only when Z_HARNESS_EXTERNAL_DEFAULT=1 (default post Phase-D flip). Tier 5: pwd/z-harness. Writes/validates <git-common-dir>/.z-harness-base anchor JSON. Emits base_resolved once per process via sentinel-guarded _z_harness_emit_base_resolved().

Stable per-repo safe basename: <repo-basename>-<8hex> where 8hex=sha256(realpath(git-common-dir))[0:8]. All worktrees of one repo produce the same id. Falls back to sha256(realpath(pwd)) when not in a git repo.
Returns <base>/active-plans — the registry home. Never inline z-harness/active-plans.
Returns <base>/active-plans/claims — directory for per-slug claim lock files (plan-claim hard mutex, orthogonal to this lockless registry).
Returns <base>/followups — the followup-sink root. Resolves dynamically so in-flight flock fds remain stable if migration runs later.

Haiku subagent. Reads SPEC.md + PLAN.md + TASKS.md (+ task block if task_id given). Emits JSON [{path, confidence, reason}]. Confidence: explicit > inferred > broad > unknown. Mechanical **Files:** parse documented as offline fallback.

Best-effort SIGTERM/SIGKILL cleanup for the per-run hang-check watchdog using the authoritative .watchdog.pid file; registry watchdog_pid is observability only. CURRENTLY DEAD CODE in production: since commit 4216c05 (2026-06-21) retired the daemon-poller watchdog in favor of a one-shot schedule-hang-check.sh, nothing writes .watchdog.pid, so pid_file.exists() is always False and this is a guaranteed no-op.

invariants: Lockless registry is safe ONLY because overlap is advisory — no code may make overlap a hard gate without replacing lockless delete with compare-and-delete or a registry lock.
Never invert the followup_common.py lock order — the registry takes NO global lock and cannot participate in the per-entry→global ordering.

Single-writer-per-record — each <run-id>.json is written ONLY by the process that owns that run; subagents RETURN data, orchestrator performs writes. claim, release, and wait-for only touch the caller's own record. reap is the one documented exception (marks peers stale).
Base anchor enforces split-brain prevention — all processes of a repo MUST agree on base; mismatch emits base_mismatch_detected and hard-fails before any artifact write.
No mutation of the base while a run is live — migrate-plan-layout.sh refuses if active-plan-registry.py list shows any status:running record.
Z_HARNESS_BASE_DIR bypasses the anchor entirely (TRUE ESCAPE HATCH); non-absolute path is a hard error.
All path construction goes through plan-path.sh helpers — inline z-harness/ literals are forbidden.
heartbeat does NOT recreate absent records — missing record → registry_error(reason:missing_record) + return 0 (no zombie records with empty fields).
claim persists only the WON set — a tiebreak loser's record MUST NOT contain the conceded path; post-wait-for re-claim is a genuine acquisition, not a dedup no-op.
wait-for clears waiting_on on EVERY exit path (via finally) — no paused zombie is ever left behind, including on SIGINT.
Release is per task, not per merge — leases are dropped on each task's clean success, not when the branch merges.

Live-local-pid carve-out: a confirmed-alive local pid past 2x stale is marked status:stale but NOT deleted — requires integer pid + os.kill(pid,0) success. Missing/non-int pid does NOT qualify for the carve-out.

watchdog_pid/_sigterm_watchdog are NOT a load-bearing dependency of any command — as of 2026-06-21 (commit 4216c05) nothing writes the .watchdog.pid file, so the field and cleanup helper are inert; do not add new behavior that assumes they fire.
gotchas: Z_HARNESS_BASE_DIR bypasses the anchor — two sessions with different Z_HARNESS_BASE_DIR values will partition their registries silently; the anchor exists to prevent exactly this.

Z_HARNESS_REGISTRY_ENABLED=0 makes overlaps, claim, release, wait-for, register, heartbeat, update-scope, reap, and deregister silent no-ops; list and session-id still work. Do not use in multi-session interactive environments.

Reaper live-local-pid carve-out: a slow-but-alive local process past 2x stale is marked status:stale but NOT deleted — its leases remain active until the pid dies. A wedged senior with live pid will block juniors for their full budget before they abort. Resolution: manually run 'python3 scripts/active-plan-registry.py release --run-id <peer-run-id> --all' after confirming the peer is genuinely stuck.

v1 records (schema_version < 2 or missing held_paths) are lease-incapable: _is_lease_capable returns False. Such peers contribute to soft scope overlap only; they are never waited on via wait-for. Missing held_paths is NEVER 'holds nothing'.
scope_extractor Haiku fallback (mechanical **Files:** parse) produces only explicit confidence entries — inferred/broad entries require the Haiku model.

Overlap comparison is path-string equality only (normalized repo-relative); no glob or prefix matching. Two tasks editing the same file but named differently in scope arrays will match; tasks editing different files won't.

The anchor is written atomically only if absent — if two sessions race on a brand-new repo, one wins and the other reads the winner's anchor. This is correct; both will independently resolve the same base tier.
Z_HARNESS_STRICT_OVERLAP=1 + Z_HARNESS_REGISTRY_ENABLED=0 is a contradictory config: strict mode has no effect when registry is disabled. No error is emitted; strict mode silently does nothing.

heartbeat on a missing record emits registry_error(reason:missing_record) and returns 0 — it does NOT recreate the record. Zombie records with empty slug/session/repo_id would pollute overlap detection. There is no --waiting-on CLI flag on heartbeat — paused-beat writes go through _set_waiting_on() inside wait-for.

session-id on macOS uses a pure-Python <ppid>-<current_epoch> fallback (no /proc); repeated calls from different tool invocations get different tokens. Export Z_HARNESS_SESSION_ID once at run start to stabilize.
held_conflict in overlaps output is a TOP-LEVEL flat array, NOT nested inside each peer entry. It is absent (not present as empty array) when no held-path conflicts exist.

Two distinct wait budgets exist — Z_HARNESS_AUTO_WAIT_BUDGET_SECS (300s, auto-park for unattended runs) and Z_HARNESS_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECS (1800s, explicit interactive wait). They are NOT the same knob. On exit 10 (timeout): waiting_on is cleared, status=running restored, LOUD wait_timeout emitted. Never silently proceed on exit 10.
Z_HARNESS_WAIT_REQUIRE_MERGE=1 is reserved/deferred — the branch-ancestor cleared logic is NOT wired. Leave at 0. The operative cleared signal is deregister-only.

run_id ordering is LEXICOGRAPHIC string comparison, NOT chronological by started_at. started_at is display-only. The _is_senior helper is the single authoritative predicate — never use started_at for ordering comparisons.

_reap_inline() is the wait-for-internal reaper. It is NOT the same callsite as cmd_reap (the subcommand). Both share the same deletion/carve-out policy but _reap_inline takes a pre-resolved active_dir to avoid repeated plan-path.sh subprocess calls in tight poll loops.

register/heartbeat --watchdog-pid and _sigterm_watchdog are DEAD CODE in current production paths: since commit 4216c05 (2026-06-21, 'cutover to scheduled hang-check, retire daemon poller') deleted watchdog-spawn.sh/watchdog-sweep.sh, nothing writes <plan>/active/<run-id>.watchdog.pid and no SKILL.md caller passes --watchdog-pid. deregister's _sigterm_watchdog call is a guaranteed no-op. The commit message explicitly flags this for later cleanup — left in place to avoid registry-schema churn. The live watchdog mechanism (schedule-hang-check.sh / hang-check.sh / notify-watchdog.sh) is entirely decoupled from this registry.

events.name: plan_marked_stale
events.description: Record marked status:stale (remote/unknown-host at 1x threshold, or live-local-pid at 2x threshold).

events.name: lease_claimed
events.description: Lease acquired; payload includes claimed paths and any conceded paths with holder_run_id.

events.name: lease_released
events.description: Paths removed from held_paths; payload {run_id, paths}.

events.name: wait_started
events.description: Entering poll loop behind one or more senior peers.

events.name: wait_timeout
events.description: Budget expired before targets cleared (exit 10). LOUD. Caller must not silently proceed.

events.name: wait_interrupted
events.description: SIGINT/SIGTERM received during wait loop (exit 130). waiting_on always cleared via finally.

events.name: scope_overlap_detected
events.description: Path intersection found between own scope and a peer scope.

events.name: active_plan_scan_complete
events.description: Overlap scan completed; no advisory or blocking overlap found.

events.name: registry_error
events.description: Non-fatal internal registry error (e.g. missing_record on heartbeat). Always returns 0.

events.name: base_resolved
events.description: Base tier resolved and anchor written/validated. Emitted at most once per process via pid-keyed stamp file.

events.name: base_mismatch_detected
events.description: Anchor path differs from freshly-resolved path — hard fail before any artifact write.

events.name: coordination_warning
events.description: Write-set validation (F5) — an implementer touched an undeclared path that a LIVE peer holds in its held_paths; consumed from overlaps --json held_conflict payload. Review-blocking but advisory; exactly one per colliding (path x peer); zero when uncontended. NOT emitted by active-plan-registry.py itself.

events.name: plan_migrated
events.description: Artifact moved (or metrics merged) from in-repo source to external base. Payload: {item, from, to[, mode:append]}.

config_keys.note: All registry and wait/lease knobs are ENV-ONLY — read directly from os.environ at use-site in active-plan-registry.py or plan-path.sh. They are NOT TOML config keys and are NOT emitted by config.py export-env. config.py inspect-all surfaces them under the 'env-only' category for discoverability.

base_and_registry.description: Controls whether external tiers 2-4 are active. 0 opts out to in-repo behavior (tier 5 only).
Explicit absolute override for artifact base. Bypasses anchor entirely. Must be absolute.
Set to 0 to make claim, release, wait-for, register, heartbeat, update-scope, overlaps, reap, deregister silent no-ops (for CI). list and session-id still work.
Seconds after which last_heartbeat is considered stale. Reaper deletes at 2x margin for dead/remote; marks live local pid as stale only (carve-out).
Set to 1 to make explicit×explicit exact scope-path overlaps a hard halt (exit 20). Does NOT affect held-path conflict behavior.

wait_and_lease.description: 1 = auto-park behind a senior held-path conflict using wait-for with the auto budget. 0 = restore interactive proceed/wait/abort menu for held conflicts.
Wall-clock ceiling (seconds) for auto-park mode. On expiry: wait-for exits 10 (LOUD timeout), orchestrator aborts task or prompts user. Distinct from WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECS.
Seconds between poll iterations inside wait-for. Each iteration beats heartbeat, runs reap inline, and rechecks targets.
Hard ceiling (seconds) for an explicit interactive wait (user selected wait in the overlap menu). Distinct from AUTO_WAIT_BUDGET_SECS.
Reserved/deferred. When 1, a target would be cleared only when its branch is an ancestor of HEAD. Not yet wired. Leave at 0.
